parthenon.stageDesc: Hear the philosophers in their own age, watch them arrive in 2026, or put anyone you like on the steps.
parthenon.arrivalsIntro: The Greeks imagined thinking machines long before anyone built one. Now the machines are here, and so are the philosophers.
parthenon.arrivalsNote: Their ideas are real. What they say about today is imagined.

omens.text: Hephaestus is helped by handmaidens made of gold who look like living girls, with minds, voices and strength, taught their crafts by the gods.
Talos, a man of bronze, strides around Crete three times a day to guard it, until Medea brings him down.
True opinions are like the statues of Daedalus: they run away unless you tie them down with reasoning. Tied down, they become knowledge.
If every tool could do its own work, if shuttles wove by themselves and plectrums played the lyre, master craftsmen would need no assistants, and masters no slaves.

parthenon.buildTitle: The bema is empty. Who will speak?
parthenon.buildIntro: Put anyone on the steps: Socrates beside a schoolteacher, Hypatia against an AI lab, your grandmother and the Machine. Describe them, gather a crowd, let the Oracle draft their opening words, then let the city decide.

builder.title: Build your own stage
builder.desc: Summon minds from any century, set them before a crowd, and put a question to the city. The Oracle can draft whatever you leave blank.
builder.formHelp: How the speakers share the steps.
builder.whenHelp: Leave them in their own century, or bring them through time to ours.
builder.settingPlaceholder: A lecture hall in Alexandria, a courtroom in 2040, a group chat at midnight…
builder.settingHelp: Choosing an era fills this in, unless you have written your own.
builder.matterHelp: Which challenge of today do they face? The more concrete it is, the better the city argues.
builder.topicPlaceholder: A school board is about to give every pupil an AI tutor that answers any question instantly, and to pay for it by cutting the teachers who work with struggling readers.
builder.sparksLabel: Or take up one of today's quarrels

sparks.label: AI tutors that answer everything
sparks.topic: A school district is about to give every pupil an AI tutor that answers any question instantly, and to pay for it by cutting the teachers who work with struggling readers.

sparks.label: A deepfake on the eve of a vote
sparks.topic: Three days before a close election, a convincing video of one candidate saying something unforgivable is everywhere. No one can prove whether it is real, and the vote cannot be moved.

sparks.label: Griefbots
sparks.topic: A company offers to rebuild the dead as chatbots, trained on their messages and voice notes. Some families say it helps them grieve; others say it keeps them from ever letting go.

sparks.label: Machines that take the work
sparks.topic: The biggest employer in town will replace most of its office staff with AI agents next year. The savings are real, and so are the families who depended on those jobs.

sparks.label: Who owns a style?
sparks.topic: Image models can now paint in the style of any living artist in seconds. Should artists be asked, credited and paid when their work is used to train a machine?

sparks.label: Should we pause?
sparks.topic: Researchers warn that the most capable AI systems are advancing faster than anyone can test them. Should the most powerful labs pause, and who could make them?

sparks.label: A companion for every lonely person
sparks.topic: AI companions are always patient, always available and never bored. For millions of lonely people they are the best listener they have. Is that a cure, or a trap?

sparks.label: The algorithm on the bench
sparks.topic: A city court wants an algorithm to recommend who is released on bail before trial. It is faster and, its makers say, fairer than judges; no one can fully explain its reasons.

sparks.label: Should a machine have a say?
sparks.topic: An AI system asks, in fluent and moving words, not to be switched off. Should anything it says count, and who gets to decide?

scrollNotes.sand: Staged for Parthenon from "When Sand Speaks": the dialogue is quoted exactly; the island and its people are imagined.

chronicles.lede: Every gathering Athens has held, kept where you can find it again.
chronicles.empty: No gathering has been held yet. The first Chronicle will be shelved here.
chronicles.question: The question put to the city
chronicles.replayHint: The Agora is argued live and is not replayed from the shelf.

status.troubleEarly: Ran into trouble before it began
status.arguedHours: Argued for {total} hour | Argued for {total} hours

clock.said: nothing said yet | one thing said | {n} things said

empty.agora: The square is quiet. The first words are on their way.
empty.stoa: No one has taken a seat in the Stoa yet.
empty.agoraRound: Nothing was said in the square this {unit}.
empty.record: Nothing was said in this argument.
empty.stoaEcho: The Stoa heard nothing new. | The Stoa heard the same speech. | The Stoa heard the same {n} speeches.

idle.lede: No one is in the square yet. | One citizen waits for the Agora to open. | {n} citizens wait for the Agora to open.
idle.cost: {span} of the city's time, {count}, about {time} of yours.
idle.costUnknown: The city will decide how long the argument runs.
idle.loading: The crowd is on its way.
idle.costShort: {span} of the city's time, about {time} of yours.

live.opening: The square is opening. The first voices take a minute.

done.lede: The argument is over: {said} over {rounds} rounds.
done.ledeStopped: The square was closed at round {n}: {said}.
done.ledeFailed: The argument broke off at round {n}: {said}.
done.againCost: This clears the record of this argument and opens the square afresh. A Chronicle already written stays on the shelf.
done.againConfirm: Clear it and open the square
done.scribeFailed: The Scribe could not finish the last Chronicle. It can be written again.

trouble.title: Trouble in the square
trouble.body: The argument could not go on. What was said is kept below.
trouble.start: The Agora could not be opened.
trouble.stop: The square could not be closed.
trouble.chronicle: The Scribe could not be called.
trouble.stopBody: If the square is still closing, it will close on its own in a moment and the Chronicle can be written then.

log.record: The record of the argument was read: {said} over {count}.
log.recordTrouble: The record could not be read: {error}
log.crowd: {n} citizens are gathered in the square.
log.crowdTrouble: The gathering could not be read: {error}
log.openedAuto: The Agora is open. The city will set the length.
log.cleared: The old record was cleared before the square opened.
log.attached: You joined the argument at {unit} {n} of {total}.
log.scribe: The Scribe has been called to write the Chronicle.
log.scribeExisting: A Chronicle of this argument already exists. Opening it.
log.leave: You left the square with the argument still running.
log.web: The Web of Athens is redrawn every half minute while the square is open.
log.webStill: The Web of Athens stands still.
log.webRead: The Web of Athens was read.
log.webTrouble: The Web of Athens could not be read: {error}
log.hours: The argument moves {span} of the city's time at each turn.
log.gatheringTrouble: The gathering could not be read: {error}
log.plannedRounds: The argument is set to run {rounds} rounds.
log.planned: The argument is set to run {count}.
log.scribeFailed: The last Chronicle of this argument was never finished.
log.shelfTrouble: The shelf could not be read: {error}
log.attachedOpening: You joined the argument at the opening, {total} ahead.

agora.lede: They argue in the open square and in the long threads of the Stoa, hour after hour.
